data.thought: Parity failed due to a dtype promotion error when mixing numeric and string data during scoring; the translation must ensure column types match the exported bundle, casting numeric fields to float/int and handling categorical strings separately.

args.instructions: Update the Python translation to explicitly cast each column to the same dtype as in the exported R bundle: convert all numeric columns (e.g., duration.in.month, credit.amount, installment.rate.in.percentage.of.disposable.income, present.residence.since, age.in.years, number.of.existing.credits.at.this.bank, number.of.people.being.liable.to.provide.maintenance.for) to int64 or float64 as appropriate, and keep categorical columns as strings. Ensure that any intermediate NumPy arrays used for scoring contain only numeric types; separate handling of WoE lookups for categorical variables should not be combined with numeric arrays. Add preprocessing steps to coerce types before binning and WoE calculation, mirroring the R script's type handling, to prevent DTypePromotionError.
